# Dawson

![Dawson function icon](../../../../../assets/function-icons/functions/math/error-functions/07_Dawson.svg)

[Mathematics functions](../../../mathematics/index.md) · [All functions](../../../index.md)

Computes Dawson D(q)=exp(-q*q)*integral(0,q,exp(t*t),dt). D(1)=0.5380795069127684. Required x:f64, no default. ni_documented_real_v1 uses q=abs(x), never abs(result); the separate standard_real_v1 kernel uses signed x. NI-G documentation, not measured NI/NXG parity. See Detailed Help for domains, limits and FROG extensions.

## Studio authoring profile

Contract status: **partial**. The connector below describes Studio authoring; execution availability is stated separately.

<details>
<summary>Retained binding and help description</summary>

This is the source declaration, not the current measured product-execution assessment.

Evaluates Dawson D(q)=exp(-q*q)*integral(0,q,exp(t*t),dt) with a dedicated stable algorithm. Standard Dawson is odd and finite for every finite real x. D(0)=+0; D(1)=0.5380795069127684; D(2)=0.3013403889237920; D(+infinity)=+0. At large q the leading term is 0.5/q, preserving representable subnormals. Profile ni_documented_real_v1 evaluates every function at q=abs(x), including inverse domains after transformation; never applies abs to a result. Separate standard_real_v1 mathematical kernel keeps signed x and odd-function signed zero. The adapter is not globally invertible: documentary ErfC(Inverse ErfC(1.5)) is about 0.5. Profiles and version 1 are fixed by the distinct stable definition identity; no profile menu or silent change to existing operators. Required x:f64 with no default; one real result:f64, except Fresnel: cosine_integral C(x) above sine_integral S(x). FROG Highlight extension through NumericTreeMath preserves real numeric array rank/dimensions, typed empties and ordered cluster fields, promoting f32/integer leaves to f64; Fresnel produces two separate containers of the same shape. Bool, String, Path, references, error clusters, complex and Matrix are rejected. Native compiled provider is scalar f64 only; aggregates require an explicit target capability. FROG diagnostics use the existing numerical channel with no error-cluster terminals: nan_input, limit, domain, singularity, overflow, underflow, nonconvergence. Propagate NaN to every output; preserve representable subnormals, signed limiting infinities and standard odd-function signed zero. The documentary adapter maps -0 to +0. Inverse ErfC(1) is +0. Invalid real domains produce NaN with a diagnostic.

</details>

## Types and connection rules

Required x:f64 with no default; one real result:f64, except Fresnel: cosine_integral C(x) above sine_integral S(x). FROG Highlight extension through NumericTreeMath preserves real numeric array rank/dimensions, typed empties and ordered cluster fields, promoting f32/integer leaves to f64; Fresnel produces two separate containers of the same shape. Bool, String, Path, references, error clusters, complex and Matrix are rejected. Native compiled provider is scalar f64 only; aggregates require an explicit target capability.

- Type resolution: `custom_resolver`; result expression: `resolve:frog.studio.error-functions.type-resolution@1`.
- Implicit coercion: permitted by this profile.
- Arrays: accepted; lifting policy: `element_wise_same_shape_with_scalar_lift`.
- Shape rule: `preserve_x_rank_dimensions_and_ordered_fields; separate_same_shape_C_and_S_for_Fresnel`.
- Scalar lifting: no.
- Broadcasting: no.

**Input count:** 1; this contract does not enable variadic inputs.

Port order: `x`.
